headline: Healing is the body's repair system—damage triggers responses that restore function
universal_truth: Damage isn't permanent if repair systems function; recovery is built into well-designed systems
fun_facts: Your skin completely replaces itself every 2-3 weeks
Broken bones heal stronger at the break point due to extra calcium deposits
The liver can regenerate from as little as 25% of its original tissue
discussion_questions: How do you heal from setbacks?
What repair systems exist in your life?
When has damage made you stronger?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Cut yourself—you'll bleed, then clot, then scab, then heal. Often with no scar. Your body contains repair systems that activate when damage occurs. Healing isn't passive—it's active, sophisticated, and often complete.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We fear damage, but bodies are built to recover. What does the healing process teach us about resilience?

options.text: Healing requires detection, response, and resources—systems that sense damage, trigger repair processes, and provide materials for reconstruction
options.response: Yes. Healing isn't automatic—it's orchestrated. Inflammation signals damage, immune cells clean debris, new tissue grows. Recovery is a coordinated process, not magic.

options.text: Bodies just naturally return to normal
options.response: It seems natural, but healing involves complex active processes...

q1.title: Damage Detection
q1.script: Healing starts with sensing damage. Pain signals injury. Inflammation marks the site. Without detection, there's no response. Knowing something is wrong is the first step to fixing it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Damage Detection"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Repair Resources
q2.script: Healing requires resources: proteins for new tissue, energy for cell division, time for growth. Starve the repair process and healing slows. Recovery needs investment.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Antifragility
q3.script: Sometimes damage makes you stronger. Bones heal denser. Muscles grow from micro-tears. Immune systems learn from infections. Good repair systems don't just restore—they improve.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Damage isn't permanent if repair systems function. Recovery is built into well-designed systems. Trust your capacity to heal.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 247. Tomorrow, we'll explore animals that hunt—predators. Until then, consider what repair systems you have and whether they're resourced.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Repair System Check - How Do You Heal?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and strengthen personal repair systems
growTrack.activity: What are your repair systems for setbacks—emotional, financial, professional? Do they have what they need—resources, time, support? Strengthening repair capacity improves resilience. How do you heal?
